Q: How to define ObjectMapper based on autoconfiguration? A:

I found a solution by reading this migration guide.

To be able to modify the default ObjectMapper you need to create a bean of this type

@Bean
public JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer jacksonCustomizer() {
    return builder -> builder
            .defaultTimeZone(TimeZone.getDefault());
}

This way, you don't lose the autoconfiguration and can customize the objectMapper to your liking.

Then I can simply inject objectMapper into my components.

If instead you want to create a new ObjectMapper bean starting from the autoconfiguration you can do this

@Bean("customObj")
public ObjectMapper customObj(ObjectMapper objectMapper) {
    return objectMapper
            .rebuild()
            .propertyNamingStrategy(PropertyNamingStrategies.SNAKE_CASE)
            .build();
}

This way, I'll never be able to completely replace the bean that spring uses, but I'm simply creating a new "customObj" bean that I can use with @Qualifier. So the only way to change the original bean is the one indicated above.

If instead I want to create an objectMapper from scratch without considering the spring boot autoconfiguration I have to do

ObjectMapper obj = JsonMapper
        .builder()
        .configure(DeserializationFeature.FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES, false)
        .build();

Q: Kernighan and Ritchie book. If the string does not contain a newline character, then the last character of the string will be removed. Is this a bug? A:

Except that's very wasteful in terms of processing time. We know the only place newline could be, there's no need to scan whole line for it.
